<reason>CON won a competitive debate by making the clash easier to decide: carbon as a quantity harm, a vanishing-scale activity, and a “priority” that transfers nothing. PRO kept a live written-motion case (hardness without uniqueness) and answered the veto question with a directional threshold, but the concession that yachts can be equally hard plus “clean the soot and the objection survives” let CON recast the case as anti-ostentation purity rather than ordered duty. CON slightly overreached by treating uniqueness as the motion, and PRO’s clipped R1 was a real cost, but CON’s weighing and rebuttals did more damage.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s R1 break of the ivory analogy (act-harm vs quantity-harm), then closing the trap on PRO’s “both can be hard.”</best_rebuttal>
